correctness.rationale: Every selected edge has exactly one selected neighbor, forcing disjoint two-edge paths in the base graph. Signatures are the union of selected incidence sets, except selected edges have their mates as singleton signatures. Two uncovered vertices cause an empty signature (different parts) or equal center signatures (same part); a lone uncovered vertex forces every path endpoint into its own part. The converse distinguishes signatures by within-path and cross-path support. A nonmonochromatic triple-partition lemma supplies the exact largest-part existence threshold. The labeled exponential formula and the one-uncovered factorial count are derived bijectively. The standalone verifier directly enumerated all code candidates for 57 multipartite size profiles with 3≤N≤8, separately checked exact generating-function coefficients and recursive counts, and passed; infinity rests on the proof.

originality.rationale: The full exact existence criterion and cubic exponential code census for line graphs of all complete multipartite graphs are not derived in the 2017 introduction or 2021 structural/complexity treatment of the code notion. The previously established rook-graph classification is precisely the two-part specialization and is excluded as new. With three or more parts, three-distinct-part path blocks give an additional genuinely different combinatorial component type, and the sharp maximum-part condition yields a new cross-family classification. Targeted semantic record searches and primary-literature comparisons found no dominating statement. Residual priority risk from unindexed literature remains; failed searches are not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The existence and exact census of a restrictive identification code on complete multipartite line graphs are natural finite-graph invariants, not an arbitrary parameter slice. A complete classification for any number of partite classes gives a sharp maximum-part threshold, a true one-uncovered-vertex boundary, and an explicit cubic multivariate exponential formula. Three-part rainbow path blocks appear beyond the formerly known rook-graph special case; the triangular family and uniform multipartite criterion follow. The result fills a distinct structural graph-code gap even without downstream theorems.
